title: Jobs you can hand over
summary: As the shop grows you can stop doing everything yourself: Supermarket Simulator defines staff and helper items for specific jobs, including serving on the till and taking an order.
body: Hiring is not one switch for the whole shop: the game defines cashier items and helper items separately, so different jobs can be handed over individually.
Taking an order is its own task that a helper can be given, which is why restocking and serving are not the same job in the game.
Because each job has its own items, what you hand over is a decision about which burden to remove rather than a general upgrade.
What this entry does not tell you: wages, how many people you may employ or how quickly they work. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Cashier duty is tied to items of its own.
Helper duty is tied to helper items rather than to the cashier.
Taking an order is a task that can be handed to a helper.
Serving at the till stays the checkout's own behaviour.
The game ships a taskbar of its own for the jobs it hands out.
The restocker is a set of named characters of its own, with numbered models and a woman line, each with an avatar entry.
facts.evidence: asset names: Restocker_02, Restocker_03, Restocker_04, Restocker_Woman_05, Restocker_Woman_06, RestockerAvatar
